quests.opening: The bell is down there, but the moon's reflection is somewhere else. Rue says a small reflector will do. I trust Rue more than the moon.
steps: Inspect the marked source and bell target.
Rotate three supplied reflection panels to connect the light path.
Dedicate the recovered glow to the river or a traveler lantern.
quests.evidence: Server puzzle graph connects source to bell receiver; either dedication permitted; no dependence on actual nighttime.

choices.label: Return it to the river
choices.reply: The water regains a silver edge. Nell says it looks like itself again.

choices.label: Keep a little for travelers
choices.reply: A lantern holds a small silver glow. The river still has plenty left.

quests.solo_route: Personal Yard work mat with loaned tiles. Optional own-world version only after permission and snapshot validators exist; decorations never affect reward.

quests.title: The Bell Beneath the Reeds
quests.label: Story Letter
quests.opening: I know that tune. Someone taught it to me before leaving Threadlight. Perhaps the river was keeping it safe.
steps: Read the shape-captioned three-note sequence.
Reconstruct it using labeled chimes or the text sequence option.
Choose a message for the friend who left.
quests.evidence: Sequence equals authored three-symbol pattern; either accessibility input accepted; message stored and Arc B completed.

choices.label: Welcome back, whenever you come
choices.reply: Nell leaves the message by the reeds. The bell sounds once, as if it understands.

choices.label: Safe travels, wherever you go
choices.reply: Nell sends the message with the current. The bell sounds once, then lets it go.

quests.solo_route: Letter desk: all clue cards supplied; no inventory, movement timing, or paid item required.

quests.title: Seeds With Instructions Missing
quests.label: Story Letter
quests.opening: Almost, Perhaps, and Not Yet. These are peculiar seed names, but I have seen worse instructions.
steps: Compare three soil/seed-token clues.
Plant the matching seed in the deterministic practice patch.
Choose a label for its paper-leaf reveal.
quests.evidence: Seed/soil match valid; practice stage timer completes; label selected; no ordinary seed minted.

choices.label: Almost ready
choices.reply: A sentence appears on the paper leaf and stops halfway. Tansy calls it an invitation.

choices.label: Ready to begin
choices.reply: The leaf unfolds like a letter. Its roots point toward a very unfinished thought.

quests.solo_route: Deterministic personal practice patch and seed tokens. Optional freshly committed normal planting/splicing only with an accessible whitelisted route; no rare drop or real-growth wait required.

quests.title: The Flower That Hated Its Name
quests.label: Story Letter
quests.opening: It has rejected Moon Majesty, Supreme Blossom, and Kevin. I think we should listen before trying a fourth name.
steps: Compare the flower's three pictured responses.
Identify the condition that makes it open: a laughter symbol.
Choose a silly name or leave it unnamed.
quests.evidence: Three observations inspected; response inference matches clue set; naming choice accepted.

choices.label: Call it Wobblebud
choices.reply: Wobblebud opens immediately. Tansy apologizes to every formal botanical society.

choices.label: Let it stay unnamed
choices.reply: The flower opens without a label. Tansy leaves a little blank sign beside it.

quests.solo_route: Deterministic personal practice patch and seed tokens. Optional freshly committed normal planting/splicing only with an accessible whitelisted route; no rare drop or real-growth wait required.

quests.title: Rain for a Cloud in a Jar
quests.label: Story Letter
quests.opening: The cloud has watered everyone except itself. We should fix the channels, and perhaps also the arrangement.
steps: Read the cloud movement rule and three planter markers.
Route four supplied channel pieces to every target.
Release the cloud or invite it to help at the garden opening.
quests.evidence: Graph reaches all 3 targets; optional hints allowed; cloud choice stored.

choices.label: Let the cloud wander
choices.reply: The cloud leaves a soft trail of rain. It seems lighter without the jar.

choices.label: Invite it to the opening
choices.reply: The cloud reserves a spot above the watering can. Tansy adds it to the guest list.

quests.solo_route: Deterministic personal practice patch and seed tokens. Optional freshly committed normal planting/splicing only with an accessible whitelisted route; no rare drop or real-growth wait required.

quests.title: A Garden Allowed to Grow
quests.label: Story Letter
quests.opening: We have a flower, a place for rain, and an empty planter. I think the empty planter might be the most important part.
steps: Place three memory objects and one empty planter on the mat.
Keep the path open and satisfy the two marked shelter cells.
Put the empty planter at the gate or the center.
quests.evidence: Four quest tokens placed; structural/path predicate valid; planter location is one of two accepted cells; arc completed.

choices.label: At the gate for newcomers
choices.reply: Tansy leaves room beside the gate. A paper root points toward Bolt's workshop.

choices.label: At the center for everyone
choices.reply: Tansy leaves room at the center. A paper root points toward Bolt's workshop.

quests.solo_route: Personal Yard work mat with loaned tiles. Optional own-world version only after permission and snapshot validators exist; decorations never affect reward.

quests.title: Instructions for Yesterday
quests.label: Story Letter
quests.opening: The instructions are all correct. They are simply correct in the wrong order. I believe that is a smaller problem.
steps: Inspect three setup cards and visible cause/effect clues.
Arrange the cards into the valid sequence.
Choose drawings or jokes for the manual margins.
quests.evidence: Ordered answer valid; annotation choice stored; no normal craft required.

choices.label: Helpful drawings
choices.reply: The drawings explain the machine perfectly. Bolt looks a little disappointed by how simple it seems.

choices.label: Helpful jokes
choices.reply: The jokes explain the machine surprisingly well. Bolt gives the manual a comedy credit.

quests.solo_route: Loaned assembly/circuit puzzle at the Yard. Optional normal recipe route requires validated accessible recipe ID and costs; player keeps the actual crafted item.

quests.title: A Machine With Stage Fright
quests.label: Story Letter
quests.opening: It works when nobody looks at it. We have tried looking politely. Could you check the missing part?
steps: Fit four supplied parts to the calibration silhouette, or use one approved real recipe for a token.
Run the server-checked calibration diagram.
Encourage the machine or tell it a harmless joke.
quests.evidence: Assembly OR whitelisted committed recipe; calibration answer correct; choice committed; output is story evidence only.

choices.label: You can do one small thing
choices.reply: The machine prints yesterday's weather. Bolt quietly stops congratulating it.

choices.label: Why did the cog cross the road?
choices.reply: The machine prints yesterday's weather, followed by a very small ha.

quests.solo_route: Loaned assembly/circuit puzzle at the Yard. Optional normal recipe route requires validated accessible recipe ID and costs; player keeps the actual crafted item.

quests.title: The Perfect Day Problem
quests.label: Story Letter
quests.opening: I wanted to save a good day for a friend. I did not intend to prevent it from ending. Those sounded more similar in the design notes.
steps: Inspect three picnic memory strips.
Identify the earliest strip using explicit weather and object clues.
Choose to preserve the picnic's sound or its colors.
quests.evidence: Three strips inspected; chronology answer valid; bounded memory flag stored.

choices.label: Keep the sound
choices.reply: The laughter becomes a small chime in the archive. Bolt lets the rest of the day move on.

choices.label: Keep the colors
choices.reply: The colors become a small postcard in the archive. Bolt lets the rest of the day move on.

quests.solo_route: Letter desk: all clue cards supplied; no inventory, movement timing, or paid item required.

quests.title: A Useful Imperfection
quests.label: Story Letter
quests.opening: The machine can remember or repeat. I think I accidentally underlined the wrong word.
steps: Read the remember/repeat circuit labels.
Route the supplied graph to Remember, avoiding the loop.
Choose a mismatched final tile from two valid options.
quests.evidence: Graph terminates at Remember and contains no cycle; either final connector option valid; Arc D completed.

choices.label: The slightly crooked tile
choices.reply: A new postcard appears. It is imperfect and has never existed before. Bolt calls that success.

choices.label: The wonderfully odd tile
choices.reply: A new postcard appears. Bolt cannot explain its tiny hat. He decides not to fix it.

quests.solo_route: Loaned assembly/circuit puzzle at the Yard. Optional normal recipe route requires validated accessible recipe ID and costs; player keeps the actual crafted item.

quests.title: The Guest Nobody Listed
quests.label: Story Letter
quests.opening: Six place cards. Five chairs. I think we should arrange the room before deciding who does not belong.
steps: Read three seating preferences.
Arrange the five named places without conflicts, leaving a marked sixth place.
Choose a welcome card for the empty place.
quests.evidence: Seating constraints satisfied; empty-place marker preserved; welcome enum committed; solo default.

choices.label: We saved you a seat
choices.reply: Rue adds a sixth chair. The room looks more finished with an unfinished guest list.

choices.label: Come as you are
choices.reply: Rue leaves the card by the chair. Nobody asks the next guest for an explanation.

quests.solo_route: Letter desk: all clue cards supplied; no inventory, movement timing, or paid item required.

quests.title: The Smallest Possible Festival
quests.label: Story Letter
quests.opening: We do not need a grand event. We need one corner that looks happy to see people.
steps: Place six loaned structural pieces on the mat.
Connect the entry, shelter, and table markers.
Choose flags or paper stars for the final decoration.
quests.evidence: Required structural and clear-path predicates pass; decorative choice ignored by scoring.

choices.label: Paper flags
choices.reply: Pip hangs the flags in the wrong order. Rue decides there is no wrong order for this.

choices.label: Paper stars
choices.reply: One star folds itself into a moth. Rue pretends not to notice until it is ready.

quests.solo_route: Personal Yard work mat with loaned tiles. Optional own-world version only after permission and snapshot validators exist; decorations never affect reward.

quests.title: The Lantern That Waited
quests.label: Story Letter
quests.opening: The last lantern will not light for an instruction. I suspect it is waiting for an invitation.
steps: Inspect three shape-coded lantern markers or their desk-map cards.
Arrange their welcome symbols in the shown order.
Choose a preset welcome for the final lantern.
quests.evidence: Three marker IDs inspected; order matches authored path; welcome enum turns on personal quest lantern state.

choices.label: There is no hurry
choices.reply: The lantern glows slowly. Rue waits with it, just to make the point clear.

choices.label: We are glad you came
choices.reply: The lantern glows at once. Something small rustles in the paper decorations.

quests.solo_route: Fixed personal Yard clue markers, with an equivalent desk map containing the same evidence; no public-world access, speed, or social requirement.

quests.title: Leave a Chair Out
quests.label: Story Letter
quests.opening: We have brought your shelter and garden memories to the table. There is still one place left. That is on purpose.
steps: Select the already-unlocked shelter and garden postcards.
Place them at the table with the spare-chair marker.
Dedicate the chair to someone new or someone returning.
quests.evidence: A2/C4 postcard entitlements present; memory arrangement valid; dedication stored; Morrow reveal and Arc E completion.

choices.label: Someone new
choices.reply: Morrow lands on the spare chair carrying a blank page. Rue simply says hello.

choices.label: Someone returning
choices.reply: Morrow lands on the spare chair carrying a blank page. Rue says welcome back.

quests.solo_route: Letter desk: all clue cards supplied; no inventory, movement timing, or paid item required.

quests.title: Things the Moth Did Not Eat
quests.label: Story Letter
quests.opening: These scraps are not missing memories. They are the spaces around them. We may have accused the wrong part of the story.
steps: Inspect three recovered scraps.
Sort marked memories and blank spaces using visible symbols.
Choose how to greet Morrow after the discovery.
quests.evidence: Three scrap classifications valid; accessible translation available; greeting stored.

choices.label: An apology
choices.reply: Morrow folds its wings into a small bow. Mica starts a new file labeled Corrections.

choices.label: An invitation to explain
choices.reply: Morrow points to the blank page. Mica finally understands what it has been carrying.

quests.solo_route: Letter desk: all clue cards supplied; no inventory, movement timing, or paid item required.

quests.title: A Map Made of Almost
quests.label: Story Letter
quests.opening: The unfinished paths all lead somewhere. We simply have to stop insisting they were meant to be finished alone.
steps: Read four unlocked memory cards alongside their clues.
Arrange four map pieces so their marked paths connect.
Choose a name for the route back to the letter desk.
quests.evidence: Four required chapter-memory entitlements; graph reaches desk; route name enum committed; no unaided recall required.

choices.label: The long way home
choices.reply: The path reaches the first letter desk. Pip has already prepared a fresh stamp.

choices.label: The beginning again
choices.reply: The path reaches the first letter desk. The blank page is no longer empty by accident.

quests.solo_route: Fixed personal Yard clue markers, with an equivalent desk map containing the same evidence; no public-world access, speed, or social requirement.

quests.title: The Day We Did Not Keep
quests.label: Story Letter
quests.opening: A memory is allowed to stay. A day is allowed to end. We can hold one without trapping the other.
steps: Review the available callbacks from Nell's message and Bolt's picnic memory.
Place the two keepsake cards outside the Repeat loop.
Choose what the final postcard emphasizes.
quests.evidence: B4/D3 flags read with defaults; keepsake placement excludes repeat node; final keepsake enum saved.

choices.label: The people who were there
choices.reply: The postcard holds the people clearly, with room around them for what comes next.

choices.label: The possibility of another day
choices.reply: The postcard holds a bright empty corner. Mica labels it Tomorrow, not yet written.

quests.solo_route: Letter desk: all clue cards supplied; no inventory, movement timing, or paid item required.

quests.title: Dear Whoever Comes Next
quests.label: Story Letter
quests.opening: We have the first letter, the last page, and a town willing to try tomorrow. Would you help us write the address?
steps: Compose three preset lines from the seal, garden, and chair callbacks.
Read the personalized final postcard.
Sign A friend or The next courier and send it.
quests.evidence: S01–S23 completed; three allowed phrase selections; signature committed with Arc F receipt; first-completion seal unique.

choices.label: A friend
choices.reply: Morrow folds the blank space into a new envelope. There is room for another story.

choices.label: The next courier
choices.reply: Pip hands you a fresh stamp. Morrow folds a new envelope. There is room for another story.

quests.solo_route: Letter desk: all clue cards supplied; no inventory, movement timing, or paid item required.
